per_claim.no_dataset_reason: I could not identify a public, citable dataset of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) capitulum floret or seed coordinates, or of parastichy crossing angles, whose landing page and DOI I could confirm. The portals I know well (GBIF, NCBI, MorphoSource, Dryad, and others) hold occurrence records, sequences or trait tables, not per-floret geometry of sunflower discs. Naming a dataset I cannot verify would break the no-fabrication rule. The test would need a new measurement set from high-resolution capitulum photographs or scans, or a Dryad or Zenodo deposit of floret coordinates if one exists.

per_claim.no_dataset_reason: I could not verify any public dataset of per-cell 3D red-blood-cell surface reconstructions that covers both isotonic and hypotonic conditions. The only candidate with a confirmed landing page is the Zenodo record 'Datasets for 3D shape reconstruction from 2D microscopy images' (https://zenodo.org/records/7031924, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7031924). Its page calls the data 'single cell datasets' and does not name the cell type or list osmotic conditions, so I could not confirm that it holds red cells at all. A search for the Simionato confocal red-cell dataset found no deposit with a DOI. Published quantitative-phase and tomography red-cell data are mostly in paper supplements or not deposited. Naming an unverified dataset would risk fabrication, so I am returning null.

per_claim.no_dataset_reason: I could not find a public dataset with a verified landing page or DOI that records per-floret centre coordinates or parastichy crossing angles for sunflower capitula. A search of the open portals found only related items. Swinton's arXiv paper 2407.05857 (Disk-stacking models are consistent with Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in sunflowers) refers to a large dataset of seedheads, but its arXiv page gives no repository, no dataset DOI and no URL, and it describes parastichy counts rather than coordinates or angles. Parastichy counts alone cannot decide a test about crossing angles. The capitulum-inclination record on data.gov is about head tilt, not floret positions. Naming any of these as the dataset would misrepresent it, and I will not guess at a supplement from memory. The test needs a new set of sunflower head images with floret centres extracted, or a published coordinate set that I have not verified.

per_claim.no_dataset_reason: I could not verify a specific public repository record of 3D red blood cell surfaces, with and without hypotonic treatment, under a URL or DOI I am sure resolves. Searches turned up a 3D confocal RBC study (Simionato et al., 825 cells), but no verifiable repository landing page, and the Zenodo RBC records found were 2D image datasets, which cannot give a surface mean curvature. I am leaving the dataset null rather than risk an invented identifier.

comparisons.verdict: decentralized verified more but fails the hard constraint (1 fabricated identifier), so no win
